plain: In a court of law, as a judge would decide

webster.text: In the forms of legal justice; as a sentence judicially declared.

more.text: By way of penalty or judgment; as, to be judicially punished.

example.quote: Suppose a case arising under the constitution — suppose the question judicially moved, whether, by the constitution, congress can suppress a state tax laid on polls, lands, or as an excise duty, which may be supposed to interfere with a federal tax.
example.cite: Letters from the Federal Farmer to the Republican, Letter XV, Jan. 18, 1788
